reviews.comment: David Powers makes organic chemistry very interesting with his added humor and lectures. He genuinely makes you want to learn about the topics and go to class for organic chemistry. His exams are also very similar to his homework assignments which with tutoring are incredibly helpful.

Unfortunately, I don't think he will be teaching undergrad classes anymore but he was a wonderful professor for organic chemistry 1. His lectures are entertaining and are pretty much the only material covered on tests. Problem sets and PLTL sessions are super helpful.

Dr Powers is a really good professor. He is caring, genuinely funny, and knows the subject incredibly well. This course is difficult and he generally does a good job explaining what is expected. The one place he could improve is on giving consistent examples with what will be needed to know for the exam. Definitely take though

Powers will help you through Ochem!!! Trust me!! (of course remember to put in your best effort and work for this to be true). He is hilarious and makes lectures not boring. He is energetic and very passionate about his teaching so it is hard to ever really get completely confused in class!!

he's a great teacher and very funny which makes the long lectures seem less long. if you're having trouble (or even if you're not) go to office hours. he's easy to talk to and very helpful. !!do the problem sets and understand the answers, they're very similar to the exams!!
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Not an easy A and easy to fall behind if you get lost, but Powers makes ochem less scary to approach. He makes lectures fun and is good at breaking things down. A really understanding guy that genuinely cares about his students and their grades. His tests are similar to his problem sets, and he prepares you well for the exams.

Dr. Powers was seriously amazing. This class is difficult, so be prepared to study, but Dr. Powers is willing to work with you and he really wants you to pass. He is super easy to talk to both during class and office hours. Office hours are awesome because he takes our problem sets that we do for homework and will work through any question with us.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He was one of the best profs Ive had. Tests were hard and averaged below passing so dont take him if youre not a CHEM major. he was understanding with COVID and helped as much as he could. Go to PLTL if you want to do well. His handwriting was really bad so you have to listen. Luckily he curves. He was definitely easy to relate and talk to.

Dr. Powers is my favorite professor that I've ever had. His personality is a mix between a disgruntled scientist and your weekend drinking buddy. He's got a great sense of humor and will walk through any questions you have. Work hard understanding the concepts outside of class and do hard practice questions as much as you can and you'll be good.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr powers expects a lot from his students. He is very intelligent and wants his students to be also. This class requires A LOT of work to really understand the material. Our exam averages were very low, so it is discouraging. But he makes up for it in the end. Put in the work and go to PLTL!!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Powers gives great lectures. He thoroughly explains topics and while he can come off as harsh, definitely ask questions! PLTL was very beneficial. His exams were very difficult, however, he does curve significantly to account for the expected lower grades. Do practice problems and the past exams, but realize they won't be exactly the same.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are somewhat unpredictable but if you go to lecture, pay attention, and and questions it will be fine. Do lots of practice problems and dont be afraid to speak up. he likes to tease his students so dont wear your heart on your sleeve and he is pretty funny
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Powers was a great professor for organic chemistry. His lectures are great and he works through reactions on the chalk board, so going to class is really the best way to succeed. He is best reached by email and doesn't have office hours, but you can reach him if you need to.
He knows a lot and enjoys sharing the chemistry he knows. He can be very tough too, very moody.
Great prof, would recommend to anyone! His exams were challenging but fair, just put in the effort and you can get a lot out of this course.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very good at teaching material and very easy to see him outside of class. He obviously cares that we learn the material. His tests are difficult but if you are ahead of the curve you'll be fine, he is a fair prof. I just paid attention in class and skimmed the chapters/ did textbook problems and I did fine.

Dr. Powers is a very nice person who cares about his students, but he should be a graduate student professor. In order to pass this class you really have to read the book and 100% understand it. The Owls aren't horrible, but, like lecture, they do not prepare you for the exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Powers graduated from Harvard, so it without a doubt he knows his stuff and expects work to be done. Lectures were engaging, but pretty confusing to keep track of the notes he handwrites on the chalkboard. The online homeworks were quite long but helped! His exams were pretty tricky. Be ready to work hard for your grade by reading, for example.

Lectures are very informative, using material from the book and from his own experiences to keep the class interesting. Course concepts are quite difficult, so tuning out is not an option. Dr. Powers did seem confused by the lack of questions in lectures, but it was due to his MASSIVE amount of office hours and that he explains everything so well.
Pretty good instructor, explains everything well. Also does curve, but at the end of the semester, 80% is an A

OWL assignment due every week. Sucks at lecturing. Posts an exam review but then doesn't post an answer key to it so you never know if you get the answer right or wrong. His exams are nothing like the review & he says he uses questions that he gave when he taught at Harvard. The class average for exams is usually a 60 & he doesn't curve. DON"T TAKE
